a-fold-does-not-report-the-registrys-con.text: A fold does not report the registry's configuration output as a skipped request.

Issue 799, part of the work before the first stable release. This page is for a folder (anyone who folds a registry's pending requests), for the integrators who read fold receipts, and for the people who review the pull request. It follows the batch fold ticket.

story.text: As a folder, I run open-datum fold on any open datum registry and the receipt lists under skipped only holders that were requests, or looked like requests, and that the fold did not take. The registry's configuration output is never among them. When a skip appears, it means something went wrong with a request: it could not be decoded, it belongs to another registry, it is held at a key address, or it could not be folded in the observed state.

Today every fold of every registry lists the configuration output as skipped, with the reason a malformed request gets. A reader cannot tell this permanent, expected output from a request that really failed to decode, and the published demo has to explain the skip in its step text and accept exactly one skip in its receipt check.

refusals-and-limits.text: Naming the configuration output with --pending is still refused as not a pending registration.
No new skip reason is added and none is removed.
The demonstration repository follows after the release and is not touched here.

Position against the formal model: the fold selects and spends the same outputs, so the change has no consequence the model observes. A search of the model finds no declaration that names skipped accounting.
